text:
Rachel: Hey team — OrbitFlow reported they can't see their API key in the console after we finished onboarding. They signed up this morning; console shows no keys under their project. Customer is blocked from testing.

Diego: Looking. Do we have the tenant_id/org_id and the onboarding run id? Also, did we emit any provisioning errors in the claim logs?

Rachel: tenant_id=org_03kL9, org_name=OrbitFlow, onboarding_id=onb_20260315_78. I checked the provisioning service: it returned 201 for the API-cred creation but the admin audit log shows project=test-internal. Screenshot attached by customer (they DM'd) shows empty key list in "orbitflow-prod" project.

Diego: ugh — that smells like the OIDC claim mapping mismatch we saw last week where the id_token "project" claim came back as the staging/test project. Can you paste the provisioning log lines?

Rachel: pasted log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z onboarding-service INFO created_api_cred id=cred_8b9f project=test-internal tenant=org_03kL9 requested_by=onboard-worker
2026-03-15T10:05:12Z provisioning-service INFO claim_processed claim.project=test-internal claim.iss=https://idp.partner.local
2026-03-15T10:05:13Z console-sync WARN project_lookup_mismatch tenant=org_03kL9 expected=orbitflow-prod resolved=test-internal
```

Diego: Okay that's consistent. Two possible causes: 1) the OIDC token mapping for this partner is returning the wrong project claim (their IdP mis-configured), or 2) our onboarding flow used a cached test token. Quick repro: run admin query to list api creds for that tenant across projects:

```
# run as infra-admin
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/tenants/org_03kL9/creds?scope=all"
```

That should show cred_8b9f and the project it's attached to. Can one of you run and paste output?

Jules: I ran the query. Result: `{"creds": [{"id":"cred_8b9f","project":"test-internal","status":"active"}]}`

Rachel: Customer is saying they did not expect test-internal and they need the key in orbitflow-prod. Can we rebind the key to the correct project without rotating it? Customer doesn't want rotation right now.

Diego: We have an internal tool `onboardctl` that can reassign project binding for a credential if it's purely metadata and not HSM-bound. Command:
```
onboardctl rebind-key --cred-id cred_8b9f --from-project test-internal --to-project orbitflow-prod --reason "onboard claim mismatch"
```
But we need infra approval because it writes directly to the metadata DB and we must update audit and sync caches. @Jules can you run this and then trigger console-sync?

Jules: I'm on it. Running with extra guard: will snapshot metadata then rebind. Running now.

(deploy-bot): action requested by Jules: snapshot metadata for tenant org_03kL9 -> completed

Jules: rebind complete. `onboardctl` output: `OK rebind cred_8b9f -> orbitflow-prod (audit=audit_9921)`. Now triggering console-sync and cache invalidation.

(deploy-bot): console-sync job queued (job_id=cs_5542).

Rachel: I pushed the resolution steps to the support ticket and asked OrbitFlow to refresh their console (ctrl+F5) and re-open the project.

OrbitFlow-SRE: Confirmed — I can see the API key now in orbitflow-prod. Thanks! Using it to test calls now.

Rachel: Great. Customer reported their app now gets 200 on requests. They asked why this happened. Diego, can we add a short postmortem note / root cause and a guard so newly created creds can't be assigned to non-matching projects?

Diego: Root cause: the partner IdP sent a `project` claim that maps to a staging project name; onboarding-service didn't validate that the claim matched the org's canonical project namespace. Fix: add validation check in onboarding-service to assert claim.project resolves to the tenant's registered project OR fail the onboarding run. Also add a fallback that rejects creation into "test-*" projects unless explicitly allowed by a feature flag. I'll open a PR and add an automated check in the pre-create hook.

Jules: I'll also add a short DB constraint that prevents creds from being orphaned into projects outside an org's allowed set — this will guard against future manual reassignments that don't go through onboarding flow.

Rachel: Filed a support follow-up note: customer offered to share IdP admin contact; we're looping them in if needed. Closing ticket after 24h confirmation. :white_check_mark:

Diego: PR link posted internally: https://git.internal/redwood/onboarding/pulls/482 — includes unit tests for claim validation and a migration to deny defaulting to projects with prefix "test-".

Jules: Post-action: audit event created (audit_9921) and retention logged. Customer-facing message drafted.

Rachel: Customer confirmed they completed end-to-end test and everything is green. Marking thread resolved. Thanks team. :tada:
